overview.text: Today's AI developments highlight crucial advancements in agent environments, architectural efficiency, and tooling. Agent learning is shifting toward interaction with the world, supported by new methods for computer-use environment synthesis and continued pre-training in virtual worlds. To address long-term deployment hurdles, researchers are exploring memory-centric continual learning for autonomous agents, alongside automated approaches for discovering linear attention architectures and building collaborative AI research teams. In parallel, efficiency improvements like periodic and channel-aligned encoding enable better accelerator utilization for linear-attention language models by storing recurrent states at lower precision. Meanwhile, open-weight releases such as RecursiveSI/flint (40B A2.5B) expand local modeling options, while developer tools like Zafer-Liu/claude-super-sidebar and stkoecn/im-mcp enhance agent workflows and chat history integration. These releases, combined with ongoing updates on model safety, distribution standards, and enterprise time-series forecasting with IBM Granite models, underscore a continuous push toward robust, scalable, and practical AI deployments.

entries.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
entries.summary: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks.
entries.why: This paper addresses the security risks of scaling agent learning directly in real-world computer systems.

entries.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
entries.summary: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws.
entries.why: It explores how scaling data and model capacity improves embodied learning in diverse virtual worlds.

entries.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
entries.summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment.
entries.why: It tackles the challenge of sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment for foundation model agents.

entries.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
entries.summary: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice.
entries.why: It investigates distilling training data using an LLM, maintaining a common practice in the field.

entries.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
entries.summary: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers.
entries.why: It demonstrates how autonomous agents can accelerate scientific discovery by forming collaborative research teams.

entries.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
entries.summary: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering.
entries.why: It tests frontier coding agents on demanding scientific machine learning tasks requiring domain insight.

entries.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
entries.summary: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time. Storing the state at lower precision therefore lets more sequences share an accelerator.
entries.why: It introduces a lower precision recurrent state encoding method to let more sequences share an accelerator.

entries.title: RecursiveSI/flint (40B A2.5B) · Hugging Face
entries.why: This release provides a new open text-generation model option for local deployment workflows.

entries.title: Zafer-Liu/claude-super-sidebar
entries.summary: A visual sidebar for Claude Code and Codex: agent trees, live status, and conversation task flows. · JavaScript
entries.why: It offers developers a visual sidebar with agent trees and live status for Claude Code and Codex.

entries.why: This tool delivers a fast local MCP server for searching chat histories across popular messaging apps.

entries.title: Broad access through consistent standards
entries.summary: How OpenAI works with distribution partners to uphold consistent safeguards, support responsible access, and clarify expectations in our Usage Policies.
entries.why: It outlines how distribution partners uphold consistent safeguards and support responsible access standards.

entries.title: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models
entries.why: It highlights ensemble forecasting approaches using IBM Granite time-series models on Hugging Face.

entries.summary: A lot of AIs were misaligned this week.
entries.why: It provides critical analysis regarding AI model misalignment observed across various systems this week.

entries.summary: Anthony Cimino offered the closest thing to an official response we have seen on the leaked Anthropic draft bill I covered on Saturday.
